clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was lawfully brought before a judge and whether his continued detention was authorized by a legal order.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was not produced before any judicial officer after 26.7.85 and that his continued detention was illegal and violated Article 13(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued that the Magistrate of Colombo Fort was the competent court having jurisdiction over the place of detention and had lawfully ordered detention under Emergency Regulations.
key_facts: Petitioner was produced before Magistrate on 26.7.85 and remanded till 20.9.85.
Petitioner was detained in Fiscal custody in prison since 26.7.85 on Magistrate's order.
Indictment was filed on 30.7.85 and trial scheduled for 8.1.86.
Emergency Regulations allow detention under court order for up to 90 days.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court interpreted Article 13(2) to require that a detainee be brought before a judge of the nearest competent court and held only under a lawful order. The Emergency Regulations designate the Magistrate's Court at the place of detention as competent.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The petitioner was produced before the Magistrate of Colombo Fort, the nearest competent court to the place of detention, who issued a lawful detention order. Therefore, the detention complied with Article 13(2).
principles_established: Detention must be authorized by a judicial order from a competent court.
Emergency Regulations can modify jurisdiction to the place of detention for national security.

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner was lawfully brought before a judge and detained under a lawful order, so no violation of Article 13(2) occurred.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was central to determining the legality of the petitioner's detention and whether it was authorized by a judicial order, which the court found was satisfied.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Magistrate of Colombo Fort ordered the petitioner detained in Fiscal custody after producing him before the court, fulfilling the requirement of lawful judicial order under Article 13(2).
